items.title: Make the two radial controls immediately readable
items.what: On the portrait gameplay screen, the lower third is dominated by two dark circular pads labeled only "STANCE" and "TECHNIQUE"; the idle pads show tiny center dots and faint arrow glyphs, but no visible drag direction, attack intent, or active-state affordance.
items.why: A first-time phone player cannot confidently tell whether to tap, swipe, or hold, and the low-contrast rings make the primary interaction look decorative rather than touchable.
items.how: Add a one-time touch hint directly above the pads (for example, "DRAG TO MOVE" and "DRAG TO STRIKE"), use four brighter directional wedges, and show a short animated thumb movement on first entry; keep the warm palette but raise the default control contrast.

items.title: Teach the first playable move before the countdown ends
items.what: On the pre-fight "QUALIFIER / Vs HasanAbi" screen, the instruction banner at roughly the upper-middle says "PATIENT. HE WAITS FOR YOUR WIND-UP — THEN MAKES YOU PAY." It gives strategy flavor but never explains that the right stick direction plus stance direction produces a named technique.
items.why: The player reaches the fight knowing an opponent tip but not how to perform an attack, so the first round can feel unresponsive or opaque on a touch device.
items.how: Replace or supplement the banner on the first bout with a two-step visual hint such as "DRAG TECHNIQUE UP + STANCE RIGHT = FRONT KICK," then highlight the two relevant stick directions during the countdown; show the flavor advice after the first successful input.

items.title: Make the boot screen communicate real loading progress
items.what: On the ShoeMoney pre-boot screen, the text "Downloading the game" sits above a long horizontal bar that appears essentially empty, with no percentage, transferred amount, or estimated state.
items.why: During the highest-risk abandonment moment, an empty-looking bar makes a functioning load resemble a stalled browser page and gives the player no reason to keep waiting.
items.how: Bind the bar to actual asset progress, fill it visibly from 0%, and add a compact status line such as "Loading dojo... 42%" or "Preparing fighters..."; show a distinct completion state before transitioning.

items.title: Give the result screen a clear way out
items.what: On the "HASANABI WINS" result screen, the only prominent action is the large "REMATCH" button near the bottom, while "STARTING IN 8" indicates an automatic continuation.
items.why: A player who wants to stop, review controls, or leave after losing is pushed toward another bout and may miss the narrow interaction opportunity before the countdown advances.
items.how: Add a secondary "EXIT TO DOJO" or "MENU" button beside or below Rematch, pause the auto-rematch countdown when the result screen is tapped, and make the chosen path explicit with separate primary and secondary styling.

items.title: Use the available browser width instead of leaving a dead black field
items.what: In the supplied wide-browser gameplay capture, the dojo and fighters occupy only the upper portion of the page, the two controls shrink to small pads at the extreme bottom corners, and a large unused black area fills the lower half.
items.why: The composition reads as a broken or unresponsive layout outside the 390x844 portrait baseline, and the reduced controls become harder to use despite having abundant screen space.
items.how: Add a wide-viewport layout breakpoint: scale the arena to fill the available stage height, place the controls in a consistent bottom control rail with a usable minimum diameter, and constrain the entire game surface to a centered aspect-ratio container instead of stretching the portrait HUD into empty space.
